ἐπικαλύψῃς ἐφ' αἵ ματι τῆς σαρκός μου, μηδὲ εἴη τόπος τῇ κραυγῇ μου· καὶ νῦν ἰδοὺ
ἐν οὐρανοῖς ὁ μάρ τυς μου, ὁ δὲ συνίστωρ μου ἐν ὑψίστοις. Ἀπορούμενος πρὸς τὴν
γῆν διαλέγεται, 365 καὶ εἰς συμπάθειαν ἐκκαλούμενος λέγει ῥή ματα, ἃ καὶ εὐκτικῶς
εἴρηται. Λέγει δέ· Μὴ σιωπήσῃς, ὦ γῆ, τὰ κατ' ἐμὲ, μηδὲ συγ κρύψῃς τὸ ἀδίκως
ἐκχεόμενον αἷμα ἐκ τῆς σαρκός μου διὰ τῶν ἰχώρων· μηδὲ στῇ ἐν τόπῳ καὶ
ἀποκρυβῇ, μηδὲ εἰς λήθην ἔλθῃ τὰ κατὰ τοὺς ἐμοὺς ὀδυρμούς· πολλοὶ δὲ, φησὶν,
οἰκοδομήθωσαν διὰ τῶν ἐμῶν πειρασ μῶν. Ἢ μὴ γῆ κρύψῃ μου τὸ αἷμα, ἀλλ' ἐκ
καλέσηται τὸν Θεὸν εἰς ἐκδικίαν, αὐτοὺς τοῦ σώματος τοὺς ἰχῶρας ἔχουσα
μάρτυρας. Καὶ ὁ ἀὴρ μὴ ἐπισχοίη μου τὴν κραυγὴν, ἀλλ' εἰς οὐρανοὺς φθάσοι τῆς
φωνῆς ὁ τόνος, ἵνα ὁ Θεὸς τῶν γινομένων κακῶν ἔκδικος κατα στὰς, καὶ τοὺς
αἰτίους ἀμυνόμενος, οὕτω γοῦν ἅπασι δείξῃ τῶν ἐμοὶ βεβιωμένων τὸ ἄμεμπτον. Τὸ
δέ· Ἰδοὺ ἐν οὐρανοῖς ὁ μάρτυς μου, καθαρωτάτης ἐστὶ συνειδήσεως. Κεφ. ΙΘʹ, γʹ.
Γνῶτε μόνον ὅτι ὁ Κύριος ἐποίησε με οὕτως. Εἰς φόβον αὐτοὺς καταφέρει, οἱονεὶ
λέγων· Μὴ οὕτως ἐπεμβαίνετέ μοι κάμνοντι, μηδὲ ὑμεῖς τοῖς αὐτοῖς περιπέσητε, τὴν
αὐτὴν ἔχοντες φύσιν. δʹ, εʹ. Ναὶ δὴ ἐπ' ἀληθείας ἐγὼ ἐπλανή θην· παρ' ἐμοὶ δὲ
αὐλίζεται πλάνος, λαλῆσαι ῥήματα ἃ οὐκ ἔδει, τὰ δὲ ῥήματά μου πλα νᾶται, καὶ οὐκ
ἐπὶ καιροῦ. –Ἔα δὲ ὅτι ἐπ' ἐμοὶ μεγαλύνεσθε, ἐνάλλεσθε δέ μοι ὀνεί δει. ∆εδόσθω,
φησὶν, καθ' ὑπόθεσιν ὅτι πε πλάνημαι. Παρ' ἐμοὶ δὲ αὐλίζεται πλάνος· πλάνος ὁ
διάβολός ἐστιν. Τίς ὑμῖν, φησὶν, ἐκ τούτου βλάβη, ποία δὲ ἀνάγκη κρίνειν ὡς ἀσεβῆ,
καὶ ἐπεμβαίνειν πάσχοντι; δέον συγγινώσκειν ὑπὸ ἀλγηδόνων φθεγγομένῳ. –Εἰ καὶ
τοιαῦτα ἐπεποιήκειν οἷα οὐκ ἔδει, 366 ἆρ' οὖν ἐχρῆν ὑμᾶς οὕτω μοι ὀνειδίζειν; – Καὶ
δέον με, φησὶ, πάλαι εὐσεβείας ἐπιμε λούμενον, νῦν τὴν ἐκ τῶν ἔργων ἔχειν παῤ
ῥησίαν. Τοῦτο μὲν οὐ πεποίηκα, κρίνομαι δὲ ὡς πλάνος. Ἐπιβάλλει καὶ ὧδε· ʹ, ζʹ.
Γνῶτε οὖν ὅτι ὁ Κύριός ἐστιν ὁ ταράξας· ὀχύρωμα δὲ αὐτοῦ ἐπ' ἐμὲ ὕψωσεν. Ἰδοὺ
γελῶ ὀνείδει, οὐ λαλήσω. Κεκράξομαι, καὶ οὐδαμοῦ κρίμα. ∆ιαλογίζεσθε, φησίν· οὐκ
ἀπὸ σκοποῦ ἀλ γύνομαι, καθάπερ τειχίῳ τινὶ τοῖς δεινοῖς κυκλούμενος. Λέγω, φησὶν,
μετὰ ἀληθείας, ὡς ἔχει τὰ κατ' ἐμὲ, καὶ οὐ παραδέχεσθε τοὺς λόγους. Τὸ γὰρ ἐν
ὀνείδει, ἵνα εἴπῃ τὰ πράγματα. Τὸ δὲ οὐ λαλήσω, ἀντὶ τοῦ· διὰ τὸ ἀντιλέγειν μοι
ὑμᾶς δοκῶ μηδὲν εἰρη κέναι. –Εἰ δὲ καὶ πρὸς τὸν Θεὸν βοήσω, εἰς φανερὸν ἅπασιν
ἐνέγκαι τὰ κατ' ἐμὲ, οὐ τυγχάνω τῆς ἱκεσίας. Οὐδεὶς ἀκούει, οὐ δεὶς δικάζει, οὐδένα
βλέπω, οὐκ ἔχω ποῖ ἀπελθεῖν. Ταῦτα ἐλεῆσαι οὐ χρῆ; –Τοι γαροῦν ἀφήσητε, οὕτως
ἀκρίτως μου κατη γοροῦντες, μήποτε Θεὸς εἰς κρίσιν κασταστή σῃ, εἰς πράξεσθαι
ὑμῖν δίκην ἀλόγου θρα σύτητος. –Οὐ γὰρ ἀνεύθυνα, φησὶ, τὰ τοιαῦτα καταλιμπάνει
Θεός. Ἔσεσθαι γάρ φησιν, εἴτε κινηθείη καθ' ὑμῶν, ὡς ἀνονήτως ὑμῖν ἐμφαίνεται ἡ
ἐπὶ γνώσει τοῦ καλοῦ οἴησις, καὶ ἡ ἐπὶ τοῖς προσοῦσιν ἄδεια. – Α. Σ. Τί φατε [ὅτι] ἐν
πονηρίᾳ ὢν ταῦτα πάσχω, καὶ ὑμεῖς τὰ αὐτὰ φοβεῖσθαι ὀφεί λετε. –Ἐσπεύσατε ἂν,
φησὶ, τότε καίτοι πραγμάτων μαρτυρούντων ἐν λόγοις· ἐν λό γοις οὖν λάβεσθε ὡς
ἂν μηδὲ ὑπὸ τῆς ἀλη θείας ψηφίσασθαι ἀνεύθυνον. –Ὁ γοῦν ἑβραῖος καὶ ἁμάρτημα
λόγου ἔχει. Κεφ. Κʹ, ιʹ. Τοὺς υἱοὺς αὐτοῦ ὀλέσαισαν ἥττονες, αἱ δὲ χεῖρες αὐτοῦ
πυρσεύσαισαν ὀδύνας. 367 Καὶ οἱ πρότερον, φησὶν, ὑποδεέστεροι, τῶν τοῦ
παρανόμου παίδων καθέξουσι. ιεʹ. Πλοῦτος ἀδίκως συναγόμενος ἐξεμε θήσεται, ἐξ
οἰκίας αὐτοῦ ἐξελκύσει αὐτὸν ἄγγελος. Πάντα μὲν ὁ ἀσεβὴς πράττει ὥστε τὰ
ἀλλότρια λαβεῖν, καὶ πρὸς τοῦτον βλέπει τὸν σκοπὸν τὰ γενόμενα· ἐπειδὰν δὲ
ἐγκράτης τῶν ὅλων δόξῃ, τότ' αὑτὸν εἰς ἑτέρους με ταφερόμενον ὄψεται. ιηʹ. Ὥσπερ
στρείφνος ἀμάσητος, ἀκατά ποτος. Οἱ λόγοι καὶ τὰ δόγματα [ἀσεβοῦς] στρί φινα καὶ
νόσκυα, οὐδὲν γὰρ ἔχει γλυκὺ ἐκεῖ να, τὰ κατὰ τοῦ Θεοῦ γινόμενα. κβʹ. Ὅταν δὲ
δοκῇ ἤδη πεπληρῶσθαι, θλι βήσεται, πᾶσα δὲ ἀνάγκη ἐπ' αὐτὸν ἐπε λεύσεται. Ταῦτά
φησιν· Ἕνεκα τῆς αἰτίας, ἀπόλ λυνται τὰ κτηθέντα, καὶ εἰς προγόνους οὐ
παραπέμπεται. κγʹ. Ἐπαποστείλαι ἐπ' αὐτὸν θυμὸν ὀργῆς, νίψαι ἐπ' αὐτὸν ὀδύνας.
Ἀντὶ τοῦ, ἐκ Θεοῦ καὶ ἐξ οὐρανοῦ ὑποσ τήσεται δεινά· ταῦτα δὲ ἔφη, ἐπειδὴ ὁ Ἰὼβ
φήσας ὑπὸ Θεοῦ πεπλῆχθαι, ἐμνημόνευσε καὶ ὡς ὑπὸ ἀνθρώπων ἠδικημένος· κατα
σκευάζει οὖν ὅτι πάντα δι' ἁμαρτίας ἐπ' αὐ τὸν ἐπηνέχθη. κεʹ. Ἄστρα δὲ ἐν διαίταις
pass_a_gloss: …the hills, so that he may say, you do not understand the things before creation. Chapter 16, verses 18, 19. Earth, do not cover over on the blood of my flesh, nor may there be a place for my cry; and now behold in heavens my witness, and my co-knower in the highest. Being at a loss he converses toward the earth, and calling out into sympathy he says words which are also said in wishing mood. He says: do not be silent, earth, the things about me, nor hide together the blood unjustly poured out from my flesh through the ichors (serum of sores); nor let it stand in a place and be hidden, nor let the things about my lamentations come into oblivion; but many, he says, let them be built up through my temptations. Or: let earth not hide my blood but call out God to vengeance, having the very ichors of the body as witnesses. And let the air not hold back my cry, but let the tension of the voice arrive into heavens, so that God being established avenger of the evils happening and warding off the guilty, thus at least shows to all the blamelessness of the things lived by me. And the saying, behold in heavens my witness, is of a most pure conscience. Chapter 19, verse 3. Know only that the Lord made me thus. He brings them down to fear, as though saying: do not thus trample upon me labouring, lest you also fall into the same things, having the same nature. Verses 4, 5. Yes indeed in truth I erred; with me lodges a deceiver, to speak words which were not needed, and my words wander, and not in season. Let it be that you magnify yourselves over me, and leap upon me with reproach. Let it be given, he says, by hypothesis that I have erred. With me lodges a deceiver; the deceiver is the devil. What harm to you, he says, from this, what necessity to judge as impious and to trample upon one suffering? it being right to forgive one uttering under pains. If even I had done such things as were not needed, was it then necessary for you so to reproach me? And it being right, he says, that I, long caring for piety, now have the freedom of speech from works. This I have not done, but I am judged as a deceiver. He adds also here: verses 6, 7. Know then that the Lord is the one who troubled; his stronghold he raised against me. Behold I laugh at reproach, I will not speak. I will cry, and nowhere judgement. Reason, he says: not off target am I pained, as by a certain wall encircled by the terrible things. I say, he says, with truth how the things about me are, and you do not receive the words. For the 'in reproach' so that he may say the facts. The 'I will not speak' instead of: because you speak against me I seem to have said nothing. And if also to God I shout, to bring into the open to all the things about me, I do not obtain the supplication. No one hears, no one judges, no one I see, I do not have where to go away. Is it not necessary to pity these? Therefore you should leave off, so uncritically accusing me, lest God establish you into judgement, to exact from you a penalty of irrational boldness. For not unaccountable, he says, does God leave such things. For it will be, he says, if he should be moved against you, how profitlessly appears to you the conceit upon knowledge of the good and the fearlessness about the things impending. Aquila, Symmachus: what do you say, that being in wickedness I suffer these things, and you ought to fear the same. You would have hastened, he says, then, although the facts testifying, in words; in words therefore take hold so that not even by the truth to vote unaccountable. The Hebrew at least also has sin of word. Chapter 20, verse 10. His sons may the lesser destroy, and his hands may kindle pains. And the formerly inferior, he says, will hold down the children of the lawless one. Verse 15. Wealth unjustly gathered will be vomited out; from his house an angel will drag him out. The impious does all so as to take others' things, and toward this aim look the things done; but when he seems master of all, then he will see it transferred to others. Verse 18. Like tough gristle unchewed, unswallowable. The words and doctrines of the impious are tough and (corrupt word νόσκυα), for those have nothing sweet, the things done against God. Verse 22. When he seems already to have been filled, he will be afflicted, and all necessity will come upon him. These he says: on account of the cause the acquired things perish, and are not sent on to forebears (descendants). Verse 23. May he send upon him fury of wrath, may he rain upon him pains. Instead of: from God and from heaven he will undergo terrible things; and he said these because Job having said he was struck by God, remembered also how wronged by men; he therefore argues that all things were brought upon him through sin. Verse 25. Stars in dwellings...
pass_b_english: … the hills, as if to say: you do not know the things before creation.

“Earth, do not cover over the blood of my flesh, and let there be no place for my cry. And now, behold, my witness is in heaven, and the one who shares my knowledge is on high” (Job 16:18-19). At a loss, he speaks to the earth, and calling it to sympathy he says words that are spoken as a wish. He says: Do not keep silent, O earth, about what has befallen me, and do not help to hide the blood unjustly poured from my flesh through my sores. Let it not stand still in one place and be hidden, and let my laments not pass into forgetfulness. Rather, he says, let many be built up through my trials. Or: let the earth not hide my blood but call God out to vengeance, with the very discharges of my body as its witnesses. And may the air not hold back my cry, but may the force of my voice reach to heaven, so that God, standing up as avenger of the evils being done and punishing those responsible, may in this way at least show all people that my life has been blameless. The words “Behold, my witness is in heaven” belong to a most pure conscience.

“Only know that the Lord has done this to me” (Job 19:3). He brings them down to fear, as if to say: Do not trample on me like this in my suffering, or you too may fall into the same things, since you have the same nature. “Yes, in truth I have gone astray, and a deceiver lodges with me, so that I speak words I ought not; my words go astray and are out of season. But let it be that you magnify yourselves against me and leap on me with reproach” (Job 19:4-5). Let it be granted, he says, for argument's sake, that I have gone astray. “A deceiver lodges with me”: the deceiver is the devil. What harm, he says, comes to you from this? What need is there to judge me ungodly and to trample on a sufferer? You ought to pardon a man who speaks under pain. Even if I had done such things as I ought not, should you then have reproached me like this? And I, he says, who have long cared for godliness, ought now to have the confidence that comes from works. I have not done that, yet I am judged a deceiver.

He adds here too: “Know then that it is the Lord who has troubled me; he has raised his stronghold against me. Behold, I laugh at reproach; I will not speak. I will cry out, and there is no judgement anywhere” (Job 19:6-7). Consider, he says: I am not grieved without cause, hemmed in by my troubles as by a wall. I tell you truly, he says, how things stand with me, and you do not accept my words. “At reproach” is said to name the facts. “I will not speak” means: because you contradict me, I seem to have said nothing. And if I cry to God to bring my case into the open before all, I do not obtain my plea. No one hears, no one judges, I see no one, I have nowhere to go. Ought not these things to move pity? So leave off accusing me so recklessly, or God may bring you to judgement to exact from you the penalty for senseless rashness. For God, he says, does not leave such things unpunished. For it will happen, he says, if he is moved against you, that your conceit of knowing the good and your carelessness about what lies ahead will prove to have been of no profit to you.

Aquila and Symmachus: “What do you say? That I suffer these things because I am in wickedness? Then you too ought to fear the same things.” You would have hurried then, he says, though the facts bear witness, to argue in words. So take hold of your words, so that not even the truth may vote you free of account. The Hebrew at any rate also has “a sin of word”.

“May the lesser destroy his sons, and may his hands kindle pains” (Job 20:10). And those who were formerly beneath them, he says, will get the better of the lawless man's children. “Wealth gathered unjustly will be vomited up; an angel will drag him out of his house” (Job 20:15). The ungodly man does everything so as to take what belongs to others, and all that he does looks to this aim; but when he seems to be master of everything, then he will see it carried over to others. “Like tough gristle that cannot be chewed or swallowed” (Job 20:18). The words and doctrines of the ungodly are tough and [unpalatable], for the things done against God have nothing sweet in them. “When he seems already to be filled, he will be afflicted, and every distress will come upon him” (Job 20:22). He says this: because of the cause, what was acquired is lost and is not handed on in his family. “May he send upon him the fury of wrath, may he rain pains upon him” (Job 20:23). That is: he will suffer terrible things from God and from heaven. He said this because Job, after saying that he had been struck by God, also spoke of being wronged by men; so he sets out to show that everything was brought on him through sin. “And stars in his dwellings …” (Job 20:25)
